title: Strip compat-proxy and unify persisted flag schemas
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Summary: A legacy compatibility proxy and an ad-hoc legacy-flag-mapper were introduced in early rollout phases to accept old client configs and route traffic to fallback handlers. Over time these have become maintenance burden: duplicated telemetry, increased tail latency variance, and brittle conditional logic that blocks safe schema evolution. This ticket removes the compat-proxy and migrates persisted flag keys/configs to a single canonical config-schema v2. The work includes safe migration tooling, operator controls, and a staged rollout with clear observability.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy compat-proxy binary and all HTTP/gRPC routes removed from the runtime and service mesh
Config-schema v2 is the sole accepted on-disk format; v1 reader deprecated and gated behind operator toggle
Migration scripts can perform idempotent dry-runs and produce a migration report listing changed keys
No customer-facing errors attributable to missing legacy keys during a 72h full-ramp window
Telemetry shows no net increase in P99 latency or error-rate > 0.5% vs baseline after full rollout
migration_steps: Run discovery job across S3/DB to enumerate v1 configs and generate migration plan
Execute idempotent migration in dry-run mode and publish report to migration-bucket
Perform controlled migration on a small set of non-critical Dedicated clusters
Flip runtime to reject v1 payloads only after all persisted configs migrated
Remove v1 reader code and compat-proxy from runtime in the final release
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Nightly dry-runs for 3 days and manual review of reports
Phase 1 Canary: Migrate 1-2 canary clusters (approx 3% traffic) for 6 hours
Phase 2 Staged: Expand to 20% traffic over 24h if canary stable
Phase 3 Ramp: 60% for 24h with automated health checks and human-on-call
Phase 4 Full: 100% with deprecation notice and archive of v1 artifacts
testing_plan: Unit tests for config parser and migration utilities covering edge cases
Integration tests simulating old-client requests against migrated configs
Contract tests for public API to ensure no behavioural deltas after migration
Load tests at 2x expected peak with traffic shapes that previously hit compat-proxy
Chaos test: kill compat-proxy in staging to validate graceful degradation path
recent_activity: 2026-02-16: Architecture review — agreed to consolidate mapping logic into config service
2026-02-22: Discovery job run in staging found ~1.3K v1 configs; 12 clusters with custom loaders detected
2026-03-01: Security requested verification for KMS-wrapped keys during migration; added key-rotation checklist
2026-03-08: Dry-run migration executed on two non-customer clusters; small number of malformed v1 entries reported
2026-03-12: Oncall approved canary window; Derek to execute canary on 2026-03-13
risks: Dedicated customers using custom config loaders may experience failures if not coordinated
Silent behavioural regressions for rare request shapes due to flag-key renames
Alert noise from duplicated metrics during partial rollout could mask true regressions
Edge-case malformed v1 entries may require manual remediation and slow migration
rollback_plan: If significant regressions: 1) Pause migration jobs and set 'allow_v1_configs'=true; 2) redeploy previous runtime release to affected shards; 3) run remediation to restore original keys for impacted configs; 4) communicate to customers and schedule follow-up fixes; 5) reopen canary after fixes.
notes: Notify Dedicated customers and Solutions Engineering 72 hours before any migration affecting their clusters. Ensure logs include 'compat_migration' trace ids for at least 30 days. Post-migration, run an analytics job to validate feature-usage metrics and reconcile with pre-migration baseline.
